3E.3 We should pray to be delivered from lying lips that speak contemptuously against the righteous.

precepts.text: Flee from the land of the north, meaning North America, and deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.
precepts.point: I am for peace, but when I speak, they are for war. With his smooth policies, politics, religion, and lies our people believe him, but war is in his mind, designed to destroy us secretly, the same as was done to the Indians. We are to live peaceably with all men if possible and rely on the law of this Bible.

note.label: Psalm 120: In My Distress I Cried Unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord: for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord. Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” The land of the north is North America. Zion dwells with the daughter of Babylon, and that is what David is describing: “Woe is me, that I sojourn in Mesech, that I dwell in the tents of Kedar! My soul hath long dwelt with him that hateth peace.”

The Israelites have long dwelt with Esau, Edom, the daughter of Babylon, who hate peace, hate us, and hate our guts. So the word is flee, come forth, deliver thyself.

precepts.text: Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins and receive not of her plagues; come out of Babylon.

note.label: Psalm 120: In My Distress I Cried Unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” Come out of Babylon. Our soul has long dwelt with him that hateth peace, Esau, Edom, the daughter of Babylon, and the Most High calls his people out of her so that we do not share her sins or her plagues.

That is the answer to “Woe is me, that I sojourn in Mesech, that I dwell in the tents of Kedar!”

precepts.text: Arise and depart, for this is not your rest, because it is polluted and shall destroy you with a sore destruction, yet some of our people love this place and love the oppression.

note.label: Psalm 120: In My Distress I Cried Unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest: because it is polluted, it shall destroy you, even with a sore destruction.” Dwelling with him that hateth peace is not our rest. This place is polluted and it shall destroy us with a sore destruction, so we are told to arise and depart.

Yet some of our people love this place and love the oppression, sojourning in Mesech and the tents of Kedar as if it were home.

precepts.text: The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart; his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.
precepts.point: I am for peace, but when I speak, they are for war. With his smooth policies, politics, religion, and lies our people believe him, but war is in his mind, designed to destroy us secretly, the same as was done to the Indians. We are to live peaceably with all men if possible and rely on the law of this Bible.

note.label: Psalm 120: In My Distress I Cried Unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.” That is him that hateth peace: “I am for peace: but when I speak, they are for war.” With his smooth policies, politics, religion, and lies our people believe him, but war is in his mind, designed to destroy us secretly, the same as was done to the Indians.

We are for peace. We are to live peaceably with all men if possible and rely on the law of this Bible, knowing that his soft words are drawn swords.

points: In my distress I cried unto the Most High, and He heard me. Deliver my soul from lying lips, and from a deceitful tongue. What shall be given unto thee, thou false tongue? Sharp arrows of the mighty, with coals of juniper, coals that lay waste.
